minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 13, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:02 p.m., on October 13, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 9, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title “Council Member.”

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:20 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:35 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:01
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

City Council Minutes  1  October 13, 2015
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim October 18 through October 24, 2015 To Be "Friends of Libraries Week"

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to Director of Library Services, Genesis
  Hansen.

P2.  2015 Walk Against Drugs

  The City Council received a presentation on the 2015 Walk Against Drugs from Khatra
  Molina, Crime Prevention Specialist.

P3.  Proclaim October 18 through October 24, 2015, to be "Freedom from Workplace
  Bullies" Week

  Mayor Schlicht read the proclamation which will be mailed to California Workplace
  Advocates.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Chuck Robinson, M.V.: thanked staff and the volunteers for a fun and well-organized
Grandparents Day celebration. He stated that there are 34 cities in Orange County but Mission
Viejo is the greatest due to its facilities, programs, and the staff and volunteers.

Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: announced that there will be a flu shot clinic on Thursday, November 5,
2015, from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center. She asked the City Attorney
to present fair and unbiased information on the medicinal use of cannabis at the next Council
Meeting.

Al Holguin, M.V.: shared a video which seemed to depict a woman working roughly with her
father at the Norman P. Murray Community Center. He asked that changes be made at the center
to protect the elderly from abuse.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed his concerns with ambulance rebate kick-backs and other
issues at the Orange County Fire Authority.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 6, 7, 8, and 15 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

City Council Minutes  2  October 13, 2015
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 22, 2015, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated September 11, 2015 in the Amount of $701,144.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated September 18, 2015 in the Amount of $722,432.92

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated September 25, 2015 in the Amount of $706,889.04

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

9.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2015

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2015

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  October 13, 2015
 11.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2015

  Received and filed.

12.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for August 2015

  Received and filed.

13.  Ordinance Adding Chapter 8.14 to the Municipal Code to Provide an Expedited,
  Streamline Permitting Process for Small Residential Rooftop Solar Systems

  Adopted Ordinance 15-306 Amending Mission Viejo Municipal Code, Title 8, Building
  and Construction by Adding Chapter 8.14, Relating to the Permitting Process for Small
  Residential Rooftop Solar Systems.

14.  Ordinance on Various Speed Limit Updates

  Adopted Ordinance 15-307 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

16.  800 MHz Countywide Communications System (CCCS) Next Generation Project

  Approved a purchase order in the amount of $280,629.22 to Motorola for 40 "Hot Red"
  Radios to be installed in the patrol units and police motorcycles serving the City of Mission
  Viejo.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Quarterly Check Register Report - Fourth Quarter of FY 2014-15

  Mayor Schlicht asked when the CIP registers will be available.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas noted the difficulty with creating a full
  report due to the change in financial system software. She then agreed to send the Council
  Members two separate CIP check registers, one from the old financial system for July 1 to
  September 30, 2014, and one from the new financial software for October 1, 2014 to June
  30, 2015.

City Council Minutes  4  October 13, 2015
   Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

7.  Year-End Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Twelve Months
  Ended June 30, 2015

  Council Member Sachs announced that the City has $1.8 million that can be put into the
  General Fund or used for Council priorities. He noted that he would like to set aside
  $500,000 for Economic Development, $500,000 to build a second public park restroom,
  $100,000 for the LED street lighting program, $500,000 for repair of some of the slopes
  that may be most affected by the oncoming El Nino weather conditions, and the remaining
  $200,000 for the installation of HD cameras in areas of concern.

  Staff recommended that discussion and determination of funding priorities be discussed
  with agenda item 21.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Schlicht, to receive and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing Authority
  - For the Year Ended June 30, 2015

  Council Member Sachs asked what the City has done with $794,000 in rolling reserves from
  the Series A bonds and if the City can pay the bonds down earlier with that money.

  Director Dyas responded that the rolling reserves are part of the resources in the budget on
  the revenue side and paying the bonds down for this amount would mean dipping into
  reserves.

  Mayor Schlicht asked questions regarding the Series B bonds related to the principal balance
  and Director Dyas noted that Simon Properties is the holder of those bonds and any balances
  owed on these bonds at maturity will be forgiven.

City Council Minutes  5  October 13, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to receive
  and file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Alicia Parkway to Alarcon (CIP
  225)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report
  and answered the City Council Member's questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  award contract to Horizon Construction International, Inc. (A15-57) for the Marguerite
  Parkway Median Island Improvements in an amount not to exceed $403,632.26; (2) award
  a contract to the Orange County Conservation Corps (OCCC) (A15-58) in an amount not
  to exceed $20,745.00; and (3) adopt Resolution 15-47 Recognizing Increased Revenue of
  $60,000 in grant fund 277.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS

23.  City Initiated Proposal to Change the Street Name of "Country Club Drive" to
  "Mark O’Meara Drive"

  City Manager Wilberg and Council Member Sachs presented information on the proposed
  street name change.

  The following spoke in opposition to the street name change: Alicia Mourer, M.V.
  (presented a petition with 119 signatures in opposition); Christine Saracino, M.V.; Terry
  Yapp, M.V.; Helen Stamate, M.V.; George Erickson, M.V.; and Lew Levy, M.V.

  The following presented written statements opposing the name change: Andrew
  McCarron, M.V.; Stephanie McCarron, M.V.; Arlene Spellman, M.V.; Roberto Saracino,
  M.V.; Kerry and Charles Nobis, M.V.; Tony and Samar Semaan, M.V.

City Council Minutes  6  October 13, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  introduce Ordinance 15-XXX and process as required, to change the street name of
  “Country Club Drive” to "Mark O’Meara Drive.”

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Sachs
  NOES:  Bucknum, Raths, Schlicht, and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

18.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented the report.

19.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

20.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

21.  Close out of FY 2014/15 and FY 2015/16 Budget Adjustments for Certain Revenue
  and Expenditure Accounts and Appropriated Reserves.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and answered
  the Council Member’s questions.

  By consensus, the Council agreed to postpone to the next meeting discussion of the FY 14-
  15 operating surplus of $1.8 million and discretionary reserve balances.

City Council Minutes  7  October 13, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to adopt
  Resolution 15-48 Amending the FY 2014/15 City Budget for Year-End Close Out
  Adjustments in Certain Accounts and Funds (excluding section 4.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

22.  Update on Water Conservation Efforts

  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including the Saddleback
College annual State of the College breakfast, the Designer Shoe Warehouse ribbon cutting
ceremony, the Women’s Council of Realtors annual charity event, the South Orange County
Economic Coalition update on South Orange County real estate, the Orange County Taxpayers
Association 5th annual Roses and Radishes award ceremony, and the annual League of Cities
conference in San Jose. Council Member Bucknum announced that the City’s Walk Against
Drugs and Artisan Faire will be held on Saturday, October 17 and Hometown Halloween on
October 24. She noted that this year’s keynote speaker at the Walk Against Drugs is Curtis Beach
and the theme is very special. On Friday, October 16 from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m. at the community
center, Senator Pat Bates, Congresswoman Mimi Walters and Council Member Bucknum will
host a senior scam stopper workshop and resource fair. She noted that she will be there in the
beginning but will then head to Camp Pendleton for the Tee it Up Fore Marines golf
tournament. Later that day, she will be speaking at a statewide conference for the HOA industry
on a topic called “Friend or Foe” which outlines how HOAs can work effectively with local
municipalities and districts. She also reminded residents of the upcoming wheelchair tennis
masters event and she announced that the Art Beat student competition deadline is in December
and information is available at all city facilities. Lastly, Council Member Bucknum announced
that scholarships are available for students through the Mission Viejo Activities Committee. She

City Council Minutes  8  October 13, 2015
 noted that applications can be found at the community center and it is a great opportunity,
especially for kids who are volunteering and doing service in the community.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he will be playing in the Tee it Up Fore Marines golf
tournament on Friday, October 23.

Council Member Ury

Council member Ury discussed his attendance at the League of California Cities conference
where he attended several sessions on water. One of the break-out sessions was moderated by
an attorney and a water use expert who went on and on about the new laws and the aggregation
of different jurisdictions to create a regional water plan. Council Member Ury said that he took
exception to the nature of the discussion because the legislature has done nothing to break down
barriers with environmentalists and environmental laws which keep cities from doing
improvements, especially additional surface water storage or other storage. He told the
moderator that if each South Orange County agency, for example, put in $2 million to improve
Oso Reservoir it would take two years to get through the environmental process and two major
storms would pass in the meantime. He stated that with all the bureaucracy coming down from
Sacramento the current drought is largely manmade. Council Member Ury noted that the vast
majority of California’s water is stored north of Sacramento and it is too bad that the coming El
Nino storms are not predicted to hit Northern California. Council Member Ury outlined his
attendance at the Roses and Radishes awards and he said the fun awards are the radishes because
they are given to the individuals or agencies that do things that are anti-taxpayer. Lastly, he
encouraged residents to pick up a copy of the new newspaper, The Mission Viejo Reporter. He
said it has a great throwback look to the 60s and 70s and is full of good information.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

25. City Council Member Time Limit on Comments

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he will table this matter to another meeting.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that Assemblyman Bill Brough has developed a brochure to
help veterans find out where they can go for assistance and it will be available at Mission Viejo
facilities soon. He read some text from the brochure and thanked Assemblyman Brough for
making it his mission to help veterans. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he received a letter
from a resident who is concerned with the lack of electric vehicle charging stations in the city so
he will ask staff to look into the matter. He reminded residents that the Uniqlo Wheelchair
Doubles Masters will be held at the Marguerite Tennis Pavilion from November 3 to 7, 2015, and
the Chamber of Commerce will hold its monthly mixer on October 15 at Tacos & Company from
5:30 to 7:30 p.m. Mayor Pro Tem Raths said he is very impressed with the Chamber and
President Chuck McCullough is doing a great job. He also noted that he has used about six or
seven local business after meeting the owners through his membership with the Chamber.

City Council Minutes  9  October 13, 2015
 Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht stated that all of the water cutbacks that residents are making only represent a
3% savings statewide. She said that we do have a manmade drought because there are not enough
reservoirs to capture water and more than 50% is going out to sea. She asked Council Member
Bucknum to give her some available dates so they can start their PACE ad hoc committee. Mayor
Schlicht announced upcoming events including the City’s annual Walk Against Drugs on October
17 and the 2015 Solar Decathlon at the Orange County Great Park, October 8 to 15 from 11 a.m.
to 7:00 p.m. She mentioned that some cities have threated to leave the Orange County Fire
Authority and she will submit, for the public record, her letter and an Orange County Register
article on the subject. She thanked the City Attorney for sharing a newspaper report on the 13
cities that are studying the creation of a new joint police department and she recounted that she
had an enjoyable morning with Sheriff Hutchins and Lt. NewMyer on October 10. She said that
during her own speech that day, she stated that Mission Viejo can’t focus on being number
one. The City of Irvine does that and they keep their record by police refusing to take crime
reports. She said that an Irvine police officer left and went to work for the City of Santa Ana
because Irvine wouldn’t take reports. Mayor Schlicht discussed her attendance at other recent
events including the Saddleback College annual report of the college where she learned that they
will be doing major renovation to most of the buildings as well as storm water mediation. She
attended the annual SCAT volunteer luncheon, a Meet the Mayor event with Boy Scout Troop
615, and a walk to school day and flag ceremony at Bathgate Elementary School. Mayor Schlicht
mentioned the heroic army veteran, Chris Mintz, who was shot while trying to save fellow
students in the Oregon shooting. She read the names of the victims and noted that she would be
adjourning the meeting in their memory: Lucero Alcaraz, Treven Taylor Anspach, Rebecka Ann
Carnes, Quinn Glen Cooper, Kim Saltmarsh Dietz, Lucas Eibel, Jason Dale Johnson, Lawrence
Levine, and Sarena Dawn Moore. She also expressed her condolences at the passing of former
Lake Forest Council Member, Marsha Rudolph and she closed with a quote from Mrs. Rudolph’s
memory card: “When through one woman a little more love and goodness, a little more light and
truth comes to the world, then that woman’s life has had meaning.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:27 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting in memory of the Oregon shooting victims, to Tuesday,
October 27, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 27, 2015

City Council Minutes  10  October 13, 2015
